newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: E.EUROPE CBANKS FAVOUR SMALL BANK MERGERS SAYS NBS.
newsitem.headline: E.EUROPE CBANKS FAVOUR SMALL BANK MERGERS SAYS NBS.

text.p: Eastern European central banks support mergers of small banks into larger institutions to make them more competetive in the european context, a senior National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) official said on Friday.

"I do not want to speak about concrete countries or specific banks, but I can say that merging smaller banks to larger, more competitive subjects is what the central banks in this region would like to see," Tibor Kasiak, head of the NBS's Banking Supervision Department told Reuters.

Kasiak chaired an annual conference of the Central and Eastern Europe Banking Supervision Department Association, held on Wednesday and Thursday in Bratislava. He holds the rotating chairmanship this year.

"In Slovakia, we do not want creation of more small banks, on the contrary, we will push some small local banks to strengthen their capital bases or we would support some of them to merge together," he said.
But he added that this did not apply to branches of foreign banks which have a universal Slovak banking licence.
"And, as I could understand from contributions during the conference, many other central banks from this region would favour merging smaller banks to increase their competitiveness," Kasiak added.
When asked what he considered a small bank, Kasiak said:"In our (Slovak) context, it is a bank with a basic capital close to the minimum allowed sum of 500 million crowns ($15.2 million)."
"For example, we have recently issued a licence to AG Banka to start with a basic capital of 500 million crowns, but we will definitely push them to increase it," he said.
AG Banka is owned by a consortium of four Slovak companies and will buy a Slovak branch of troubled Czech bank Agrobanka.
The NBS has so far granted 26 universal banking licences of which 13 went to local subjects.
Six of the local banks have basic capital of less than one billion crowns.
